Why 97% of My Trading Strategies Failed — And Why That's a Good Thing

If you tell a hiring manager that you fail at your primary task 97% of the time, they will probably show you the door. If you tell an investor that only four out of every hundred projects survive, they may assume the system is broken.
In quantitative trading, the opposite is true. A 97% failure rate is not proof of incompetence. It is often the clearest proof that the filter is doing real work.

Stable logic should not collapse because of microscopic path changes. Who usually fails here High-frequency scalpers, fragile news strategies, and over-optimized systems are the usual casualties.
